1 What this module does, and why the failures are the result

Module 04b returned 550 included records. This module tries to obtain the full text of each one: resolve an open-access PDF, download it, push it through GROBID to get TEI XML, and check whether the TEI carries recognisable methods and results sections. Records whose PDF is a scan rather than digital text would go to OCR.

The obvious way to report this module is a single success rate. That would waste it. Which papers we can and cannot read is not a technical footnote; it is a measurement of access inequality that bears directly on what this evidence map can see. If full text is systematically harder to obtain for one country’s literature, then any finding that rests on full-text fields is biased against that country, and the bias has a direction we can state. So everything below is broken down by country, by language and by source.

ret   <- readRDS(here::here(DIR_DERIVED, "retrieval_ledger.rds"))
tiers <- readRDS(here::here(DIR_DERIVED, "geography_tiers.rds"))
n_att <- NROW(ret)
n_dl  <- sum(ret$downloaded %in% TRUE)
n_tei <- sum(ret$tei_ok %in% TRUE)
n_met <- sum(ret$has_methods %in% TRUE)

2 The retrieval cascade

Every stage prints what it lost.

cascade <- tibble::tibble(
  stage = c("records entering Module 05",
            "candidate PDF URL resolved",
            "PDF downloaded",
            "GROBID produced parseable TEI",
            "TEI carries methods/results heads"),
  n = c(n_att,
        sum(!is.na(ret$url)),
        n_dl,
        n_tei,
        n_met)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(lost = dplyr::lag(n) - n,
                pct_of_entering = round(100 * n / n_att, 1))
knitr::kable(cascade, caption = "Full-text retrieval cascade, with losses at each stage")
Full-text retrieval cascade, with losses at each stage
stage n lost pct_of_entering
records entering Module 05 550 NA 100.0
candidate PDF URL resolved 349 201 63.5
PDF downloaded 286 63 52.0
GROBID produced parseable TEI 286 0 52.0
TEI carries methods/results heads 228 58 41.5

Of 550 records, 286 yielded a downloadable PDF (52.0%) and 286 produced parseable TEI (52.0%). The gap between those two numbers is small, so GROBID is not the bottleneck: acquisition is.

n_scan <- sum(ret$is_scanned %in% TRUE)
n_ocr  <- sum(ret$ocr_applied %in% TRUE)

0 of the downloaded PDFs were scans (near-zero extractable characters per page), so OCR fired on 0. The OCR path (ocrmac first, tesseract with fra/ara as fallback) is implemented and was smoke-tested, but this corpus never exercised it. That is itself worth stating: the open-access material we could reach is uniformly born-digital, which is a property of what is reachable, not of the regional literature. Scanned regional reports and theses are exactly the material sitting behind the failures tabulated below.

3 Why retrieval failed

fails <- ret |>
  dplyr::filter(!(tei_ok %in% TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::count(failure_reason, sort = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_of_failures = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
knitr::kable(fails, caption = "Reason for failure, over records that did not reach TEI")
Reason for failure, over records that did not reach TEI
failure_reason n pct_of_failures
no_pdf_url 63 23.9
http_403 61 23.1
publisher_blocked 59 22.3
network_error 27 10.2
landing_page_not_pdf 22 8.3
http_401 9 3.4
http_429 8 3.0
http_202 7 2.7
http_404 5 1.9
not_a_pdf 2 0.8
empty_response 1 0.4 
paywall <- fails |>
  dplyr::filter(failure_reason %in% c("http_403", "publisher_blocked",
                                      "http_401", "landing_page_not_pdf")) |>
  dplyr::pull(n) |> sum()
no_url  <- fails |> dplyr::filter(failure_reason == "no_pdf_url") |> dplyr::pull(n) |> sum()
transient <- fails |>
  dplyr::filter(failure_reason %in% c("network_error", "http_429", "http_202",
                                      "empty_response")) |>
  dplyr::pull(n) |> sum()

These group into three kinds, and they mean different things:

  • 151 records were refused by a publisher (403, 401, an interstitial landing page, or a known blocking host). The paper exists and is indexed; we are not permitted to read it.
  • 63 records had no open-access PDF location at all in OpenAlex or CORE. Not refused — simply not deposited anywhere reachable.
  • 43 failures were transient (network, rate limiting, 202 “still processing”). These are the only ones a re-run could plausibly recover, and they are a small minority.

The first two categories are structural. 214 of 550 records — 38.9% — are unreadable for reasons of access, not of technique.

4 Access inequality by country

by_country <- ret |>
  dplyr::group_by(country) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n          = dplyr::n(),
    downloaded = sum(downloaded %in% TRUE),
    tei        = sum(tei_ok %in% TRUE),
    tei_pct    = round(100 * sum(tei_ok %in% TRUE) / dplyr::n(), 1),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n))
knitr::kable(by_country,
             caption = "Full-text retrieval by search cell country (cell of origin, not verified study location)")
Full-text retrieval by search cell country (cell of origin, not verified study location)
country n downloaded tei tei_pct
EG 187 97 97 51.9
TN 137 70 70 51.1
MA 90 46 46 51.1
REGION 64 35 35 54.7
DZ 50 29 29 58.0
LY 22 9 9 40.9 
best     <- by_country |> dplyr::slice_max(tei_pct, n = 1)
worst    <- by_country |> dplyr::slice_min(tei_pct, n = 1)
thinnest <- by_country |> dplyr::slice_min(n, n = 1)
compounds <- identical(worst$country, thinnest$country)

The spread runs from 40.9% (LY, n = 22) to 58.0% (DZ, n = 50).

The thinnest cell is also the hardest to read. LY returns the fewest records (n = 22) and the lowest full-text rate (40.9%), so the two shortfalls compound. Any LY count in Module 07 is doubly attenuated, and a low count there must not be presented as a measured absence of research.

A caution on this table. country here is the search cell a record was retrieved from, not where the study was actually conducted — Module 06 stage 0 showed those diverge badly. The table is the right one for judging retrieval (the cell is what drove which publishers we hit), but it must not be read as studies-per-country.

p <- ggplot(by_country, aes(x = reorder(country, tei_pct), y = tei_pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4477AA") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d/%d", tei, n)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "records reaching full text (%)",
       title = "Full-text retrieval by search cell",
       subtitle = "Retrieval failure is a finding about access, not a processing error") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
print(p)

dir.create(here::here(DIR_FIGURES), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave(here::here(DIR_FIGURES, "05_retrieval_by_country.png"), p,
       width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 300)
ggsave(here::here(DIR_FIGURES, "05_retrieval_by_country.svg"), p,
       width = 7, height = 4)

6 What this leaves the evidence map to work with

an <- tiers |>
  dplyr::filter(analytic) |>
  dplyr::left_join(ret |> dplyr::select(id, tei_ok, has_methods), by = "id")
n_an     <- NROW(an)
n_an_tei <- sum(an$tei_ok %in% TRUE)

Module 06 stage 0 reduced the 550 included records to an analytic set of 262 records actually situated in the five countries. Of those, 121 (46.2%) have full text.

knitr::kable(
  an |> dplyr::group_by(tier) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), with_full_text = sum(tei_ok %in% TRUE),
                     pct = round(100 * sum(tei_ok %in% TRUE) / dplyr::n(), 1),
                     .groups = "drop"),
  caption = "Full-text coverage within the analytic set, by geographic confidence tier")
Full-text coverage within the analytic set, by geographic confidence tier
tier n with_full_text pct
A_named_country_corroborated 79 31 39.2
B_regional_corroborated 106 46 43.4
C_asserted_no_evidence 77 44 57.1

This is the number that shapes Module 06. Extracting only from full text would silently redefine the map as a map of the open-access subset — and this module has just shown that subset is not drawn evenly. So Module 06 extracts every analytic record, from TEI methods/results where available and from title and abstract otherwise, carries an evidence_base flag on every value, and stratifies every reliability figure by it. Fields that only full text can support are reported over the full-text stratum alone, with that denominator printed.

7 Method parameters for the supplement

parameter value
PDF sources, in priority order pdf_url captured at search time; OpenAlex best_oa_location; CORE by DOI
TEI extraction GROBID processFulltextDocument
Scanned-page test median extractable characters per page near zero
OCR engines (unused this run) ocrmac, tesseract, paddleocr
Download timeout 120 s
GROBID timeout 300 s
